messages:
Maria: heads-up — we're seeing a sustained local SSD IOPS hotspot on us-west1-gpu nodes that's blocking new GPU allocations. about ~40 pods Pending because kube-scheduler can't find nodes that meet disk-read latency SLOs.
Sam: ugh, saw that alert. which metric spiked?
Maria: iostat shows avg r/s read spikes to ~14k on /dev/nvme0n1 for several hosts. iowait up, per-node GPU attach failures in kubelet logs.
Jay: any SMART errors? thermal?
Maria: only WARNs — wear_leveling_count creeping on two drives, but not failing. dmesg has lots of: "nvme nvme0: I/O 12345 QID 0 timeout, aborting" repeated.
Lina: this lines up with the ephemeral-cleaner cron that ran at 03:10 UTC across the fleet — looks like scrub + fstrim + metadata compaction overlapped with a batch GPU scaling wave.
Rahul: can you paste the scrub schedule? might be the janitor job pattern.
Maria: ops-bot posted the job run: 
```
ops-bot: janitor-scrub started at 2026-03-19T03:10Z on group: gpu-us-west1
commands: fstrim --all && /usr/local/bin/scrub --depth=3 --concurrency=8
exit: 0 (but long runtime, ~7m on hot nodes)
```
Sam: concurrency=8 per host is probably too high for nvme bandwidth when combined with overlayfs metadata flushes.
Jenna: confirmed: logs show overlayfs fsync latencies up to 2s for small writes during that window. that's what keeps pods Pending (image pulls also slowed).
Jay: for short term can we throttle janitor concurrency and stagger start times? e.g., randomize within a 15m window instead of running fleet-wide at top of the hour.
Lina: yes, quick mitigation: change janitor kcron to `--spread=15m --max-concurrency=2` for gpu nodegroup. i'll put up a PR.
Rahul: long-term, we should consider per-node backpressure in the janitor so it checks iostat and backs off if avg await>50ms. also consider KV prefix caching in serving nodes to reduce read bursts.
Sam: other immediate workaround: route new GPU provisioning to us-central1 and set us-west1 to maintenance for 30m while scrub cleanup finishes. costly for latency but keeps the control plane green.
Maria: we've already temporarily removed two us-west1 subpools from autoscaler -> will keep paused for 20m.
Jenna: what's the correlation with disk wear? are these nodes nearing EOL?
Maria: not EOL. but we have a cohort of older 2TB drives with higher write amplification. scrub + fstrim increases internal garbage collection, which spikes host-side IOPS and exposes firmware timeout paths.
Jay: options: 1) stagger/smart-backoff janitor (cheap, fast) 2) replace older drives with higher endurance (capex, months) 3) move scratch to networked NVMe/ephemeral NVMe-attached partitions with QoS (op-ex + infra change) 4) parameterize pod scheduling to avoid nodes with high wear metric.
Rahul: let's quantify cost: replacing a drive ~ $400/drive * ~200 nodes in cohort = $80k hardware + ops. Moving to networked scratch will increase per-run egress/storage costs and add latency. Staggering janitor is 0$ and obviates most outages.
Lina: i'll open RFC for janitor-backoff and a rollout plan. short-term PR to reduce concurrency and add randomness is ready — rolling it to us-west1 first.
Sam: also suggest we expose an internal metric `node.local_nvme_pressure` and use a PodAffinity anti-affinity rule to avoid scheduling heavy-image-pull workloads on pressured nodes.
Maria: action items:
- Lina: deploy staggered janitor PR to gpu-us-west1 (in 10m).
- Sam: add node.local_nvme_pressure metric and a scheduler predicate spike (ETA EOD).
- Rahul: run cost calc for 3-year repave vs staged replacement and put in finance sync.
- Jenna: monitor SMART and dmesg patterns for 24h to validate no firmware regressions.
- Jay: update incident note with root cause = synchronized scrub + fstrim + overlayfs flush causing NVMe GC/firmware timeouts -> GPU provision backpressure.
Maria: thanks — will post updates. if you see repeated nvme timeouts, tag me and move node to cordon. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: alert cleared for us-west1-gpu scrub-run 03:17Z, but we've kept 2 subpools drained for 20m as a precaution.
Sam: nice triage — this was quick.
Maria: closing this thread after staging the PR. will reopen if we see another spike.
